DDS and appeal to the federal SSA. These parts of the proceeding allow the 
apphcant to submit additional documentation and receive further medical 
evaluation. If the claim is denied again, the apphcant may request a hearing 
before a SSA ALJ. If the ALJ affirms the denial, the apphcant may file an

2. 
Hearsay in Administrative Adjudication. Although an agency’s order 
must be supported by substantial evidence, the rules of evidence that apply in 
Article III courts do not apply in administrative hearings. See 5 U.S.C. 
§§ 556(d), 706(2)(E). One consequence is that hearsay may be admissible and 
rehed upon in an administrative hearing. Perales may be read to imply, 
however, that an agency might violate due process if it rehed solely upon 
unrehable hearsay. Courts evaluate the rehabihty of hearsay based on factors 
such as the available contradictory direct testimony, internal evidence of 
rehabihty, the form of hearsay, the reputation of its source, and the availabihty 
of corroboration. See, e.g., CommoTbwealth Unemployment Compensation Bd. 
of Review v. Ceja, 427 A.2d 631 (Pa. 1981) (decision denying unemployment 
benefits voided because of unrehabflity of hearsay evidence); Hoska v. U.S. 
Dep't of the Army, 677 F.2d 131, 138-39 (D.C. Cir. 1982) (hearsay can 
constitute substantial evidence under certain circumstances, such as when 
declarants are disinterested witnesses); Black Beauty Coal Co. v. Fed. Mine 
Safety & Health Bev. Common, 703 F.3d 553, 559 (D.C. Cir. 2012) (testimony 
based in part on hearsay can be credited over other testimony); Angov v. Lynch, 
788 F.3d 893 (9th Cir. 2015) (evaluating the rehabihty of unrebutted hearsay 
supporting a denial of asylum and related rehef). Although exclusive rehance 
on hearsay raises concerns, the “substantial evidence” test allows adjudicators 
to flexibly evaluate relevant evidence. For example, in Biestek v. Berryhill, 587 
U.S. 97 (2019), the Supreme Court held that a vocational expert’s testimony 
may count as “substantial evidence” supporting a denial of disabihty benefits 
even if the expert refuses to provide underlying private market survey data.
